questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

The authority tries to __subjugate __the marginalised people
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"liberate". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To **liberate **means to free someone from restrictions or limitations.
 
• It denotes the act of setting someone free from a state of subjugation or servitude.
 
 
• **E.g., **"The army was able to **liberate** the hostages from their captors."
 
 
 
• From the above explanation it is clear that both words are antonyms to each other. 

Therefore, the correct answer is "**Option 2".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subordinate** means to treat or regard as of lesser importance than something else.
 
• It also indicates a lower position in a ranking or hierarchy.
 
 
• **Example:** "In history, many colonial powers used their military superiority to **subordinate **native populations, imposing their culture, language, and rule upon them."
 
 
 
• Although **"subordinate" **seems related to **"subjugate," **it does not represent a direct antonym as it does not mean to free or empower people.
 
 
• **E.g.**, "She refused to subordinate her ideals to achieve political gain."
 
 
 
• **Enslave **means to make someone a slave or to** subjugate** them.
 
• It is synonymous with "subjugate" and therefore cannot be an antonym.
 
 
• **E.g., **"The invader tried to **enslave** the indigenous people."
 
 
 
• To** trap **means to catch someone or something in a place or situation from which it is hard to escape.
 
 
• **E.g., **"The mouse was **trapped **in the cage."

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.**

Hasty
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Cautious". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"hasty" **implies acting with excessive speed or insufficient consideration.
 
• In other words, it refers to a decision or action made too quickly, without taking enough time to consider the possible consequences.
 
 
• **Example: **"In their excitement to launch the product, the team made a hasty decision to skip the final testing phase, which unfortunately led to several issues that could have been prevented."
 
 
 
• **Cautious **means acting with care to avoid potential harm or mistakes.
 
• A cautious person thinks things over before acting, which is the opposite of acting hastily or rashly.
 
 
• **For example: **"He is a cautious driver, always following the speed limit and checking twice before making a turn."
 
 
 
• From the above explanation it is clear that both words are antonyms to each other. 

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reckless:** A person who is reckless shows a disregard for danger, taking risks without thought of the potential negative outcomes.
 
• This is very much aligned with being hasty, not against it.
 
 
• **For example: **"His reckless actions endangered everyone in the vicinity."
 
 
 
• **Brisk: **This word usually implies a good, quick pace.
 
• But it doesn't necessarily imply a lack of caution or consideration, it could also just mean efficient.
 
 
• **Example: **"She maintained a brisk pace during her morning jog."
 
 
 
• Quick: Quick like brisk refers to something done with speed and promptness.
 
 
• **For example: **"Her quick thinking saved the day."

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in simple past tense.**

A. Last year, I have travelled to Japan.

B. Last year, I was travelling to Japan.

C. Last year, I travelled to Japan.

D. Last year, I had been travelling to Japan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **C**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "**C. Last year, I travelled to Japan**" expresses the simple past tense.
 
• It uses the simple past tense ("**travelled**") to express a completed action in the past.
 
• It accurately conveys that the speaker traveled to Japan last year.
 
 
• **Structure of the simple past tense**: Subject + Past Simple Verb + Object__
 
• **Example**: *She visited Paris last summer.*
 
 

Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sentence A**: This sentence contains a tense inconsistency. "Last year" already establishes a past time frame, so the past simple tense should be used.
 
• **Sentence B**: This option uses the past continuous tense ("was travelling"), which implies ongoing or continuous action in the past.
 
 
• **Structure**: Subject + Past Simple of "to be" (was/were) + Present Participle Verb (-ing form)__
 
• **Example**: *I was studying when the phone rang.*
 
 
 
• **Sentence D**: This option uses the past perfect continuous tense ("had been travelling"), indicating a continuous action that was completed before another past event.
 __
 
• **Structure**: Subject + Past Perfect of "to be" (had been) + Present Participle Verb (-ing form)__
 
• **Example**: *She had been working on the project for hours before they arrived.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

The moon looks bright and beautiful in the cloudless night sky. Yet it is very small compared _______ Earth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "to". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Let's analyze each option:**

 
 
• **With:** This preposition is generally not used for comparisons of inequality (bigger, smaller, etc.).

 
 
• It doesn't fit well in this context.
 
 
 
• **Than: "Than" **is used after comparative adjectives.
 
 
• **"Compared" **usually takes **"to", **not **"than". **
 
• So this option is not correct.
 
 
 
• **To: **This option is correct.
 
 
• **"Compared to" **is a standard structure used to contrast two things.
 
• The sentence reads: **"The moon looks bright and beautiful in the cloudless night sky. Yet it is very small *compared to __*Earth."**
 
 
 
• **In: **The preposition **"in" **is used to show location or state, not to make comparisons.
 
 
• Hence, this isn't the appropriate choice.
 
 
 
 
 
• By selecting** "option 3",** the sentence is grammatically correct and clear in conveying its meaning, implying that the moon, although bright and beautiful in a cloudless night sky, is much smaller when compared to the size of the Earth.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• "**Starting**" is used as the present participle (used in present continuous or gerund forms).
 
 
• **For example**: *They are starting the project today.*
 
 
 
• "**Starts**" is used when referring to the third person singular (he, she, it) in the present tense.
 
 
• **For example**: *He starts his work early in the morning.*
 
 

*​* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• The choice between "**start**" and "**starts**" depends on the grammatical structure of the sentence and the **subject-verb agreement**.
 
• In this case, "**start**" is the base form of the verb, and it agrees with the structure dictated by the past tense modal "**would not**."
 
• Using "**starts**" (as '**he**', the third-person singular form is mentioned) in this context, would create a **disagreement in verb tense**.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Stole**

__
 
• **Stole **means to take something unlawfully or without permission. (गैरकानूनी तरीके से या बिना अनुमति के कुछ लेना)

 
 
• **Example**: *She stole a pen from the office supplies without anyone noticing.*
 
 
 
• *​*The word "**stole**" is fitting in this context because it implies that the thief took or appropriated the bicycle without permission or lawful right, given the context of criminal activity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

• **Parked**: To station a vehicle in a specific place for a period of time. (किसी वाहन को किसी निश्चित स्थान पर कुछ समय के लिए खड़ा करना)
 
• **Bought**: To acquire something by paying money for it. (किसी वस्तु के लिए धन देकर उसे प्राप्त करना)
 
• **Lent**: To temporarily give someone the use or possession of something with the expectation that it will be returned or repaid. (अस्थायी रूप से किसी को किसी चीज़ का उपयोग या कब्ज़ा इस उम्मीद के साथ देना कि उसे वापस कर दिया जाएगा या चुका दिया जाएगा)
